title: Why busy teams are slow: Queueing for Managers in five minutes

speakers.persona: Has read the book twice; explains with stories and enjoys a good number.
Runs a team, has not read it; asks the question the listener is thinking.

sections.title: The busiest team on the floor

turns.text: Here's a strange fact. The team that looks busiest is very often the one that ships the least.
Hang on — busy and slow? That sounds completely backwards.
It does, and that's the whole point of Okafor's book. Once people are loaded past about eighty percent, waiting time doesn't creep up. It explodes.
Okay, so what do I actually do on Monday morning?
You cap the work in progress. Pick a number, write it on the board, and when you hit it, nobody starts anything new until something finishes.
So the fastest way to go faster is... to start less. I love that.
